summary: Built criterion 1 only: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/DefenderState.cs reads Controlled Folder Access through a Windows PowerShell 5.1 child (20 s timeout, process tree killed, no PSModulePath) and its pure Describe turns the result into one 'Controlled Folder Access:' line, or 'not read (reason)'. HeldOpenTreeTests.Record() writes that line directly after the fsutil disablelastaccess line. Under eng/dotnet.ps1 it reads 'EnableControlledFolderAccess=0 (Disabled), protected folders=0, allowed apps=hidden from non-administrators; Defender AMRunningMode=Normal, RealTimeProtection=True, platform=4.18.26080.4'. Review M1 is confirmed by measurement: an ordinary user gets ['N/A: Must be an administrator to view exclusions'] for the allowed-apps list, so the survey's '1 allowed app' was never a count. Describe reports any list holding an 'N/A:' entry as hidden, closed as a 17-row corpus: with the plain counting the 9 placeholder rows were red and the 8 real rows green. The recipe for criteria 2 and 3 is in docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md. Q-101 stays open: nothing arms CFA or answers it. This round fixed the one architecture-rule break the engine reported: the missing-exe Fact built its path from Path.GetTempPath(), and it now uses a name under AppContext.BaseDirectory, so no temp folder is touched. The earlier full-suite run (870 of 870) predates that edit; after it, 162 tests passed in the related classes and none of the three changed files matches the rule's patterns.

files.why: The never-throwing Defender read (Run/Read, Lazy-cached Line) and the pure Describe: list counting, N/A placeholder grammar, mode names, '?' for missing properties, 'not read (reason)' for every failure.

Default-suite tests, no Trait/Skip: Describe theories for each shape, the corpus theory, real-child timeout, non-zero exit and missing-exe Facts, the PSModulePath Fact, and the Facts tying the line to a fresh read and to its place after the fsutil line. The missing-exe Fact's path now comes from AppContext.BaseDirectory, not the temp folder.

Corpus for O-017 (review M1) with 17 rows: 9 placeholder shapes and 8 real lists. It carries the measured census of 11 Get-MpPreference properties holding the N/A placeholder and the 'naive' count the design's rule gave per row.
Record() writes DefenderState.Line on the line after the fsutil disablelastaccess output; its header comment now names the CFA setting.

Line format and reading, the person's recipe for criteria 2 and 3 with the two windows, three per-run fixtures, canary and back-dated last-access witness, results table and reading key, what was rehearsed with CFA off, and what stays open.
Engine-appended settled rule 'no test or test script changes Microsoft Defender's settings' over tests/**. It was already in the tree when the build began, and the build left it unchanged.

obligations.how: DefenderStateRecordTests.TheLineAgreesWithAFreshReadOnThisPc reads the line and a fresh independent `(Get-MpPreference).EnableControlledFolderAccess` and asserts the line carries that value (0 here) in the full format, or says 'not read (' where there is no Defender. TheLineIsRecordedRightAfterTheFsutilLine pins that Record() writes it directly after the fsutil line. Run under eng/dotnet.ps1, HeldOpenTree output shows the two lines adjacent.

DefenderStateRecordTests.TheChildPowerShellStartsWithItsOwnModulePath runs a 5.1 child through the same runner and asserts its PSModulePath has no pwsh 7 entry. Under eng/dotnet.ps1 testhost does inherit pwsh 7's path (printed in the test output). With the strip removed the test goes red and the child shows pwsh 7's entries.
DefenderStateRecordTests.ANullOrEmptyListCountsAsZero feeds JSON null and [] to both lists; both print 0.
DefenderStateRecordTests.AScalarListCountsAsOneNotAsItsLength feeds a bare JSON string to both lists; both print 1.
DefenderStateRecordTests.AnArrayListCountsItsLength feeds arrays of 1, 2 and 3 entries; each prints its length.
DefenderStateRecordTests.TheModeIsNamedAndTheRawValueKept: enable 2 gives 'EnableControlledFolderAccess=2 (AuditMode)'; 0, 1, 3 and 4 are pinned too.
DefenderStateRecordTests.AnEnableValueOutsideTheKnownRangeIsKeptRawAndCalledUnknown: 7, 5, -1, 255, 1.5, "2" and true print the raw text with '(unknown)'.

DefenderStateRecordTests.AMissingPropertyPrintsAQuestionMarkAndTheRestOfTheLineStays drops each of enable, protected, allowed, mode, rtp and platform in turn; exactly one '?' appears (AMRunningMode=? and platform=? among them) and the rest of the line stays.

DefenderStateRecordTests.ANonZeroExitIsNotReadWithTheFirstStderrLine: rows including the Sandbox 0x800106ba text give 'not read (<first non-empty stderr line>)', or 'exit code N' when stderr is empty, even when stdout is valid JSON. The same-named Fact ...FromARealChild runs a real 5.1 child that writes 'boom' to stderr and exits 3.

DefenderStateRecordTests.EmptyOrUnparsedOutputIsNotRead: empty, blank, 'not json', '{', '[1,2]', 'null', '42', banner plus JSON and trailing text all give 'not read (unparsed output)'. NullOutputIsNotReadEither covers null inputs.

DefenderStateRecordTests.AChildPastTheTimeoutIsKilledAndNotRead runs a child that sleeps 30 s with a 1 s timeout. The call returned in about 1 s with 'not read (timed out after 1 s)' and the test asserts under 10 s. The test does not check the PID is gone: review M7 was waived (SC-278).

DefenderStateRecordTests.AnExecutableThatCannotBeStartedIsNotRead starts a non-existent exe; the Win32Exception becomes 'Controlled Folder Access: not read (Win32Exception: ...)'. The missing path is now built under AppContext.BaseDirectory, which creates nothing and touches no temp folder, so it no longer breaks the architecture rule 'no Core test builds a fixture in %SystemRoot%\Temp except the deliberate one'. The test passes after the change.

The new class has no Trait, Skip or Explicit. OptInTraitTests (10 of 10) and ArchitectureRulesTests.CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped (which scans the new files) pass, and so did the whole suite, 870 of 870, before the path edit. FsaDefaultTestFilter, the OptInTraitTests pin and LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests were not touched.

DefenderState.Count treats a bare string or any array element beginning 'N/A:' (ignoring case, after leading white space) as a placeholder and prints 'hidden from non-administrators'. A list holding a placeholder beside a real entry is hidden too. Only the prefix is read, because Defender's own text differs between properties (the DefaultProtectedFolders text is different). tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/DefenderStateCorpus.json holds 9 placeholder rows (P01-P09: scalar, one-element array, case, white space, reworded text, prefix alone, mixed both orders, the DefaultProtectedFolders text) and 8 real rows (R01-R08: null, [], scalar, one, several, drive N:, an entry containing 'N/A:' not at its start, \\?\ and UNC). Each row goes to both lists, and a second test recomputes the design's plain counting for every row. The census is measured and in the corpus. Before the fix, P01-P09 were red and R01-R08 green; the same split appears with the fix mutated out.

The recipe in docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md names two windows. W-admin (elevated) only reads state, arms and disarms (steps 1, 5, 7, 9). W-user (ordinary) builds, publishes, scans, runs the canary and reads events (steps 2-4, 6, 8, 10). The step 3 helper block starts by printing `whoami /groups | findstr /c:"Mandatory Label"` and throws unless it reads Medium. The results table has an Integrity column, and a row at High is void. I ran the W-user blocks from the doc at Medium.
obligations.not_mutable: A document: the fix is recipe text for a person to follow, and no default-suite test can observe it. The one executable part, the Medium-integrity guard in the step 3 paste, was run at Medium when the doc's own blocks were rehearsed.

obligations.how: The recipe now has (a) run A, a CFA-off exe scan of R-off, as the baseline, and (b) a 48 h back-dated last-access witness: three per-run fixtures R-off, R-audit and R-on, each with a sub folder, plus a control outside any protected folder. Witness is read before and after every scan, and Control must move under a plain Get-ChildItem. The reading key says unchanged means asked and kept, MOVED means fell back or never asked, and the session is void if the baseline does not read unchanged or the control does not move. Rehearsed from the doc's own blocks with CFA off, at Medium: every Witness read unchanged before and after, Control moved, scans completed with 15 files, 1 folder, 6280 bytes and 0 unreadable.
obligations.not_mutable: A document: the fix is the recipe's witness steps and reading key for a person. The commands in it ran as written against the published exe with CFA off, and that run is the only observable part.

tests.note: Baseline before any edit: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests"  (helper with the plain counting, before the O-017 fix)
tests.note: Expected: 8 failed, 56 passed. The failures were exactly the placeholder rows then in the corpus (P01-P08), which counted 1 or 2. Every real row passed.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DefenderStateRecordTests"  (after the fix)
tests.note: 64 of 64 at that run; 17 corpus rows once P09 was added.

tests.command: Mutation, applied by hand and the file restored: the O-017 placeholder check replaced by `false;`, then the corpus test
tests.note: The intended red: P01-P09 failed, R01-R08 passed. The file hash after restoring was the same as before.

Real use of the record: 'fsutil behavior query disablelastaccess: exit 0: DisableLastAccess = 2 (System Managed, Last Access Time Updates ENABLED)' is followed on the next line by 'Controlled Folder Access: EnableControlledFolderAccess=0 (Disabled), protected folders=0, allowed apps=hidden from non-administrators; Defender AMRunningMode=Normal, RealTimeProtection=True, platform=4.18.26080.4'. The pwsh 7 PSModulePath was inherited and the read worked.

870 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, exit 0. This run was before the path edit and was not repeated whole afterwards. It included RigLockScopeWordingTests over the new doc, CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped, OptInTraitTests and RuleCopiesAgreeTests.

After the temp-path fix: 162 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. This includes the missing-exe Fact and the corpus that feeds the temp-route rule's patterns. A regex check of that rule's patterns against DefenderState.cs, DefenderStateRecordTests.cs and HeldOpenTreeTests.cs found 0 matches in each. The engine's own run of the Fitness rule was not repeated by me.

tests.command: Each of the 15 discharge filters (the 13 case commands plus OptInTraitTests and CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped), run one by one
tests.note: Run before the path edit: every filter matched at least one test and passed, 1 to 17 tests each. AnExecutableThatCannotBeStartedIsNotRead passes again after the edit.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 publish src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj -c Release -o artifacts/publish, then the doc's own step 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 blocks extracted by regex and run in one script with CFA off
tests.note: Run through the real entry point (eng/read-window.ps1 against the published exe), on three fixtures under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, at Medium integrity. Each scan: EXIT 0, outcome=completed, 15 files, 1 folder, 6280 bytes, 0 unreadable. Each Witness read unchanged before and after. Control moved. The canary wrote and exited 0. Events printed nothing (CFA off). The CFA=on part was not run: it needs an administrator and a person. Fixtures and scratch files were deleted.

tests.command: powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command Get-MpPreference | Select-Object ...CFA properties (unelevated), and a census of properties whose value begins 'N/A:'
tests.note: EnableControlledFolderAccess 0, protected null, allowed ['N/A: Must be an administrator to view exclusions'], default-protected ['N/A: ... default protected folders']; 11 properties carry the placeholder.

deviations: Describe's contract expected 'allowed apps=1' on this PC. The measured value is the non-admin placeholder, so the contract's expected reading was wrong (review M1, accepted). The line now reads 'allowed apps=hidden from non-administrators', and the design note records the corrected reading.

The recipe uses three fixtures (R-off, R-audit, R-on), not the design's single R. The accepted M3 asks for a 48 h back-dated witness 'before every run, before arming'. One fixture cannot be back-dated again inside a protected folder without a write that CFA might itself refuse, so each run gets its own fixture, back-dated before arming. The control is back-dated and listed after each scan.

Describe has a sixth parameter, timeoutSeconds (default 20), so the 'timed out after N s' reason can be asserted for the 1 s timeout Fact. The runner is split into Run (returns the child's result) and Read, so tests can also run a custom script through the same environment preparation.

Two Facts were added that the design did not list, to discharge O-001 and O-002 without asserting a machine's setting: one compares the line with an independent fresh read and the other pins the line's place after the fsutil line in HeldOpenTreeTests.cs by reading that source file. The PSModulePath Fact checks what the child reports as its own path, not that the parent had a pwsh 7 path.
No outside defect is worked around, so no KnownWorkarounds entry or setting was added. The 'N/A:' placeholder is Defender's documented behaviour for a non-administrator, not a bug.
not_built: tests/window/CfaScan.ps1, its canary build and its CFA-off rehearsal log: rejected by the design. The pasteable recipe is in the design note and its ordinary-window blocks were run once as written.
An xUnit Fact that scans with CFA on, plus its Trait, filter clause and OptInTraitTests pin: rejected by the design.

Criteria 2 and 3 themselves, and Q-101: they need an administrator and a person at the desktop, and the Sandbox cannot run Defender. They are filed as the person's run; none of the CFA=on steps (the W-admin steps, the refused canary, the 1123/1124 message shapes, the notification) was run.
O-020 / M4, using C:\Users\Public\Documents as the primary fixture: waived, carried to SC-275.
O-021 / M5, a case-insensitive Defender-settings rule that also covers eng/**: waived, carried to SC-276. The rule appended by the engine is unchanged.

O-022 / M6, the PSModulePath strip and the 'case 2 is non-material' wording: waived, carried to SC-277. The strip is built as designed. The runner follows VolumeUsageTests.GetVolumeUsed (async reads, timeout, tree kill), and the class comment says so.
O-023 / M7, exposing the child's PID so the timeout Fact checks it is gone: waived, carried to SC-278. The Fact checks the returned text and elapsed time under a 30 s sleeper.
O-024 / M8, listing the allowed apps by name before and after the session and voiding on an existing match: waived, carried to SC-279. Step 1 does list both lists by name, as M1's fix asks.
The 'once per test process, in parallel' case (C-013) is not tested: the design judged it performance only. The static Lazy gives it.
follow_ups: Run the recipe in docs/design/SL-101-controlled-folder-access.md as an administrator at the desktop (criteria 2 and 3). Fill the results table and read it with the key. That is the evidence for Q-101.

If a result is 'blocked, fell back' or shows a notification caused by the scan, decide the behaviour. Options: skip the keep-last-access open in CFA-protected folders (a KnownWorkarounds entry: one checkbox, on by default, with the in-app notice) or reopen Q-159.
Exercise TryOpenKeepingLastAccess when the write-attributes open succeeds but SetFileInformationByHandle(FileBasicInfo) fails. It needs a seam in Core's open path and was not exercised by spike #109.
Repeat the CFA run on Windows 10 and on a Defender platform later than 4.18.26080.4 (Q-205, Q-224).
The five waived minors are on the backlog as SC-275 to SC-279 (Public\Documents fixture, case-insensitive rule over eng/**, spawn-idiom wording, PID-gone check, allowed apps before and after).

Not measured: whether ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders is replaced by the 'N/A:' placeholder for a non-administrator once it is non-empty (it reads as an empty list on this PC). Describe handles both. The elevated step 1 listing in the recipe will show it.
